name_note: The species was moved out of Bacteroides, so most papers before about 2020 call it Bacteroides vulgatus.

sentences.text: Phocaeicola vulgatus, originally classified as a Bacteroides species, is one of the most abundant and widespread bacteria of the human gut microbiota.
It is noted for its ability to degrade many plant-derived heteropolysaccharides.
It is closely related to, and often confused with, Phocaeicola dorei, and both are reported as important members of the infant gut microbiome.
Strains carry a mobile plasmid encoding an antibacterial toxin, BcpT, largely restricted to this species and Phocaeicola dorei.
An engineered strain carrying an oxalate degradation pathway has been tested as a live therapeutic candidate against hyperoxaluria.
